flags.detail: Found by session ab951e4c while merging origin/main on 2026-11-20. Resolution: the trunk's artwork is what cards and product pages show, because its captions describe each specific unit; this pass's five remain as guide header art, one per guide where it fits; every trunk PNG was converted to the same optimized 1200×750 q82 JPEG profile, so assets/img went from 20 MB to 2.3 MB and both sets are cheap. Both clocks remain wired (the Python one is what the gate and measurement.html use); consolidating them is a follow-up.

Do not generate a third illustration set for a product that already has one — check assets/img and data/products.json first. flags.title: The reader-capture form could submit an address into a URL when scripting was blocked
flags.detail: Found by the independent second gate (tools/audit.mjs, rule A7) while reconciling this merge, and confirmed by reading the markup: the form carried action=measurement.html method=get with a named email input. With scripting blocked, pressing Subscribe navigates to measurement.html?email=you@example.com — the address then sits in the reader's history and in whatever request log the static host keeps, while the copy on the page said the address goes nowhere. Nothing was ever collected by us; the leak was the browser's own fallback path.
flags.action: Fixed 2026-11-20 (session ab951e4c): the form now posts to no destination (action="", novalidate) and the input has no name attribute, so a no-script submission has no key/value pair to carry — an address cannot enter a URL or a request log. The counter still fires, because it reads the event, not the field. The field's own note on the page states the reason in plain words.
flags.source_note: No Amazon clause governs a form that collects nothing; this is the site's own accuracy duty — the copy said 'sends your address nowhere' while the markup had a path that could carry it. Recorded under the same principle as S36 §6(a) (do not misdescribe what your site does).

flags.detail: search.html reads results from ?q= so a search can be shared or reloaded, and the form is a GET with a named input. The measurement page's 'never stored: search query text' row is true of this site's counter (and of a site that stores nothing), but a reader could reasonably read it as 'what I type never appears anywhere', while the host serving the page can log the URL it was asked for.
flags.action: The measurement table now states the exception in the row itself and carries a plain note under the event table. No code change: the URL is the mechanism that makes search work without a server, and removing it would break shareable searches.
flags.source_note: Program Policies §3 makes the site owner responsible for accurate disclosure of what is collected and how; the fix is accuracy of the claim, not a new feature.

flags.title: The independent second gate could not read single-quoted ids and reported 52 phantom broken fragments
flags.detail: tools/audit.mjs rule A6 scans each page for id="..." in double quotes; the source register rows in verification.html were emitted with id='src-S01' in single quotes. Both are valid HTML. The result was 52 'unresolved fragment' findings against links that resolve in every browser — the kind of false positive that trains a reviewer to ignore a gate. It also meant that any tool reading only double-quoted ids is blind to that page's anchors.
flags.action: Both sides fixed (2026-11-20, session ab951e4c): the builder now emits double-quoted ids for the register anchors, consistent with the rest of the page, and the audit accepts either quoting style with a comment saying why. A6 is now clean for the right reason — the references resolve, and the tool can see it.
flags.source_note: Internal only — a tooling blind spot found while merging; the second gate's finding was wrong but its disagreement with the primary gate was worth chasing, which is why it exists.

flags.title: The second gate read an inline-JS string as a link and reported a phantom unresolved reference
flags.detail: After the id-quoting fix, tools/audit.mjs rule A6 still reported one broken reference: search.html → '+h.url+'. That is a JavaScript expression inside the page's own search script (it builds result links at runtime), not a published href. A checker that treats every quoted string in a page as a file path will keep inventing findings out of client-side code, and a gate that cries wolf gets ignored. Provenance note: this flag's own first draft quoted a builder expression literally and tripped the leak rule — the wording was changed rather than the rule loosened.
flags.action: Fixed in the audit (2026-11-20, session ab951e4c): a value containing quote/concatenation/template characters is recognised as a runtime expression and skipped, with the reason commented at the site of the change. The site itself needed no change, and the separate rule that fails when an un-interpolated builder expression leaks into static output is untouched — this only stops A6 mistaking JS for markup.
flags.source_note: Internal only — a second-gate false positive, recorded because the honest response to a gate finding is to prove which side was wrong.

flags.title: Third register-id collision inside one day: ids were allocated by guessing what other sessions would use
flags.detail: This branch claimed S27…S28, FLG-026…FLG-040, SG-21…SG-28 and Q-22…Q-26 against a board read at session start. Nine other PRs merged while it worked. Round one: the trunk already held S27, SG-21…SG-28 and Q-22/Q-23 for other findings, so this pass renumbered to S30, SG-39…SG-42, Q-24…Q-27, TP-15…TP-20. Round two (PRs #40…#48): the trunk had *also* taken those slots — S30…S35, SG-39…SG-42, Q-24…Q-25, TP-15…TP-18, FLG-026…FLG-029 — so the same rows needed new ids again. Renumbering at merge time is correct, but it is bookkeeping a machine can do, and each round is a chance to leave a reference pointing at another session's row.
flags.action: Closed structurally rather than by care: scripts/alloc_ids.py allocates ids from the merged tree at commit time and rewrites a row's own references with the same map, and scripts/check_site.py now fails any file (data, scripts, markdown, generated HTML) that cites an S/FLG/SG/Q/TP id absent from its register. This pass's fifteen flag rows are the first test of both.
flags.status: fixed by tooling; allocation discipline enforced by the gate
flags.source_note: Internal only — a coordination defect in this repository's own ids, found by the merge process itself.

flags.title: The suggestions register had a four-row gap that a live citation pointed into
flags.detail: Found on 2026-11-20 by scripts/alloc_ids.py --check, the reference audit added in this merge. The register runs from SG-01 up to SG-50 but the numbers 23, 24, 25 and 26 were never issued (an earlier session's numbering jumped), and the FSIS temperature-chart source row's access note told a reader to re-check the figures 'see the two suggestion rows numbered 24 and 25' — a pointer into a hole. Gaps like this are invisible to a count-based check and to anyone reading only the top of the file.
flags.action: The citation was corrected to name the duty that actually exists (the freshness clock and the stale-read removal flag) rather than inventing three rows to fill a gap whose intended content nobody recorded. The four hole numbers stay empty on purpose: ids are allocated from max+1 by scripts/alloc_ids.py, so a gap is never silently reused for something else. Read a missing number as never-issued, not as deleted.
flags.status: found and closed at the reference; the gap is left as evidence
flags.source_note: Internal only — a register-integrity finding from this repository's own ids, surfaced by tooling added in the same merge.

flags.title: A committed merge-conflict marker had shipped inside the executive summary
flags.detail: Found on 2026-11-20 while writing this pass's summary section: main's EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY.md contained a conflict region left in place by an earlier merge — a marker line, a one-line HEAD side, a separator, and 196 lines of main's own history inside the block. Markdown renders that as literal '<<<<<<< HEAD' text, and nothing in either gate looked at it, because both gates check the generated HTML and the registers, not the repository's prose. Nothing was lost: the 196 lines were the only copy of three earlier sessions' sections.
flags.action: Resolved losslessly by this pass: the three marker lines were removed and both sides kept, after checking that no heading in the block was duplicated elsewhere in the file. A rule was added to scripts/check_site.py so any committed conflict marker in HTML, JSON, markdown, Python or CSS fails the build — the class of defect, not the instance.
flags.status: fixed; caught structurally from now on
flags.source_note: Internal only — a repository-state finding on main, found by reading the file rather than by trusting the merge.
